packageRules.description: An x.y.0 release waits 10 days instead of 3 (ADR-0098). The pattern also matches a `v` prefix and a range such as `>=1.2.0`.

agentdev-devcontainer is built by this repository's own pipeline, so its edge digest bumps skip the release-age wait and the daily window (ADR-0098). The pin lives outside the CI image path filter (devcontainer-compose-pins.yml), so merging a bump cannot retrigger the build that produced the digest and bump itself again. Workflow jobs that run in the dev container pin the same digest, and the group moves every reference.

The base image publishes only `edge`, so Renovate moves its digest. A bump edits the image Dockerfile, which rebuilds and accepts the image from the new base before it can merge. That is what makes automerge safe here.

The image's pinned tools, including the checksum-carrying downloads, and the macOS bootstrap's pins of the same release tools, so a tool's Linux and macOS pins move in one pull request. The post-upgrade script recomputes every checksum in the same commit as the version and fails the branch when it cannot, so no bump leaves a pin half-updated. That is what makes batching and automerge safe here.
uv and Bun are pinned where the image's base does not reach: the setup-python-venv action input CI runs on, and the cloud-session startup script. Grouping each keeps its pins in one pull request.

customManagers.description: Versions of the checksum-carrying tools in docker/devcontainer/pinned-tools.yml: an entry's `version:` field, quoted or not, under a `# renovate:` comment that may name a versioning scheme for prefixed tags.
Release-tool versions in the macOS bootstrap: a `typeset -r` constant under a `# renovate:` comment that may name a versioning scheme for prefixed tags.

Versions in the image Dockerfile's `ARG <NAME>_VERSION=` lines and the cloud-session startup script's `<NAME>_VERSION = '...'` constants, each under a `# renovate:` comment that may name an extractVersion.
npm packages the local pre-commit hooks run through `bunx --package <name>@<version>` or `bunx <name>@<version>`.
